name: HVAC Technician
description: HVAC technicians install and repair heating, ventilation, air conditioning and refrigeration — and in Florida that is year-round work on the systems that make buildings usable. ⚠ It pays the best median of the clock-hour trades on this site ($61,010) and is the only one federal projections call much faster than average.
credentialNote: ⚠⚠ TWO credentials, and they work differently. **EPA Section 608 is federal law**: anyone who maintains, services, repairs or disposes of equipment that could release refrigerant must be certified (Type I, II, III or Universal), with an apprentice exempt only while closely and continually supervised. Get it during the programme. **And Florida LICENSES the contractor** under Chapter 489: Class A air-conditioning contracting is unlimited, Class B is capped at 25 tons of cooling and 500,000 BTU of heating in any one system. ⚠⚠⚠ That licence — not the certificate — is what lets you pull permits, contract and run a business, and it requires DOCUMENTED EXPERIENCE. Start recording yours from the first job rather than reconstructing it at year six.
bodyHtml:
What the work actually is

O*NET: install or repair heating, central air conditioning, HVAC or refrigeration systems. Its task statements are the service call — discuss heating or cooling system malfunctions with users to isolate problems or to verify that repairs corrected malfunctions; test electrical circuits or components for continuity, using electrical test equipment; repair or replace defective equipment, components or wiring; lay out and connect electrical wiring between controls and equipment.

⚠ Notice how much of that is electrical. People come to this trade expecting refrigeration and find that most faults are electrical — controls, capacitors, contactors, boards and wiring. The refrigeration circuit is the part that is regulated; the electrical circuit is the part that breaks.

Projected need

O*NET, on federal projections: 425,200 employed (2024), growth “much faster than average (7% or higher)”, 40,100 openings a year, and median wages $61,010 (2025) — $29.33 an hour.

⚠ That is the best combination on the trades side of this site: the highest median of the clock-hour trades here, and the only one whose growth is called much faster than average. In Florida the reason is not subtle — air conditioning runs most of the year, equipment fails in the heat, and the installed base keeps growing.

⚠⚠ Two credentials you cannot work without, and one that lifts the ceiling

EPA Section 608 is federal law. Technicians who maintain, service, repair or dispose of equipment that could release refrigerants must be certified — Type I for small appliances, Type II for high-pressure, Type III for low-pressure, or Universal for all three. An apprentice is exempt only while closely and continually supervised by a certified technician. ⚠ The certification does not expire, and every programme worth attending puts you through it.

⚠⚠ Florida LICENSES the contractor — and this is the difference between this trade and the others on this site. Under Chapter 489, Florida Statutes, air-conditioning contracting is a licensed occupation with two main classes: Class A, unlimited, covering central air conditioning, refrigeration, heating and ventilation; and Class B, limited to 25 tons of cooling and 500,000 BTU of heating in any one system. A certified contractor may work anywhere in the state; a registered one only in the jurisdiction that qualified them.

⚠ So the career has a visible ceiling and a visible door through it. You can work your whole career as a technician for someone else; the licence is what lets you contract, pull permits and run a business — and it needs documented experience, so start recording it from your first job.

⚠⚠⚠ The framework moved and most colleges have not — two live course families

Florida's current framework is HVAC/R, 1,350 hours, five completion points: Introduction, Fundamentals, Service Practices, Intermediate Service Practices, then the advanced technician courses. It is also published as a 750-hour first half and a 600-hour second, which is the structure to ask about if you need to earn while you train.

⚠ But the course numbers tell a different story about what is actually taught:

  • The current framework's own courses (ACR0000, ACR0001, ACR0012, ACR0013) are carried by four to six institutions.
  • The predecessor family — helper, then a sequence of mechanic courses (ACR0041, ACR0043, ACR0047, ACR0049) — is carried by 22 to 25.
  • ⚠⚠ No institution carries both. The two advanced courses, ACR0044 and ACR0045, are the bridge: they appear in the new framework and in the old family, at 24–25 institutions.

⚠ So the state has moved ahead of the colleges, and both versions are real training. A third family again — ACR0941–0946, Air Conditioning I to VI — runs at six state colleges as a credit-bearing sequence. Register by the programme and its hours, never by the course number, and if you transfer, take the syllabus and the hours.

Necessary skills

  • Electrical diagnosis first. Meters, circuits, controls and ladder diagrams. ⚠ This is the skill that separates a technician from a parts-changer, and it is most of the work.
  • The refrigeration cycle, properly understood — pressures, temperatures, superheat and subcooling. Charging by gauge and by measurement, not by feel.
  • Brazing and sheet metal. Joints that hold a vacuum, ductwork that moves the air you designed for.
  • Customer work. Most calls happen in someone's home or business, often in a bad moment. Explaining the fault and the price is half the job and all of the repeat business.
  • Heat tolerance and care. Attics and roofs in a Florida summer are the working environment, and heat illness is a real occupational hazard rather than a slogan.

Advice

  • ⚠ Get EPA 608 while you are in the programme, and take Universal rather than a single type if the programme offers it — the core test must be proctored for Universal.
  • Ask how many hours you spend on live equipment, and whether the programme has commercial refrigeration as well as residential split systems. Commercial and refrigeration work pays more and is harder to learn on the job.
  • Record your experience from day one. The contractor's licence requires documented experience, and people who decide at year six that they want it spend a year proving what they already did.
  • ⚠ Florida's demand is year-round and storm-driven — replacement after a hurricane season, new construction, and the commercial refrigeration that every grocery and restaurant depends on. Service work in this state is not seasonal in the way it is further north.
  • Consider NATE or HVAC Excellence certification on top of EPA 608 — voluntary, but employers use them to sort applicants and some manufacturers require them for warranty work.
